# Problem 1 - Tidyverse: New Zealand

## Load data

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
nzge_url = "https://phuongov.github.io/stats506-f26/data_f26/nzge.rds"
if (!dir.exists('p1')) dir.create('p1')
if (!file.exists('./p1/nzge.rds')) download.file(nzge_url, './p1/nzge.rds')
```

```{r}
nzge <- readRDS("./p1/nzge.rds")
```




## Process data

a. Generate a table (which can just be a nicely printed tibble) of vote count (regardless of party) per year/type. Make sure to sort it by vote count.

```{r}
result.a <- nzge %>% 
  select(election_year, voting_type, votes) %>%
  group_by(election_year, voting_type) %>% 
  summarise(total_votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_votes))

tibble(result.a)
```





Focus only on the 2014 election. Report the proportion of votes for each party in the Candidate election. Again, produce a nice table and sort it by percent of vote.

```{r}
result.b <- nzge %>%
    filter(election_year == 2014, voting_type == "Candidate") %>%
    select(party, votes) %>%
    group_by(party) %>% 
    summarise(total_votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") %>% 
    arrange(desc(total_votes)) %>%
    mutate(vote_proportion = round(total_votes / sum(total_votes), 6)) %>%
    select(party, vote_proportion)

tibble(result.b)
```





Produce a nice table indicating, for each year, which party won the Candidate vote and which party won the Party vote.

```{r}
result.c <- nzge %>%
  group_by(election_year, voting_type, party) %>%
  summarise(total_votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  filter(total_votes == max(total_votes)) %>%
  select(election_year, voting_type, party) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = voting_type, values_from = party)

tibble(result.c)
```
